title: The cubical open-box pair homeomorphism
statement: Let $I=[0,1]$ with its usual topology. For $n\geq0$, give $I^n$ its product topology and put $\partial I^n=\{u\in I^n:\text{some coordinate of }u\text{ equals }0\text{ or }1\}$; thus $I^0$ is a point and $\partial I^0=\varnothing$. Set $J_n=(\partial I^n\times I)\cup(I^n\times\{0\})\subset I^n\times I$. Every displayed subset is equipped with its subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]. There exists a homeomorphism $h_n:I^n\times I\to I^n\times I$ such that $h_n(I^n\times\{0\})=J_n$. Equivalently, the pairs $(I^n\times I,I^n\times\{0\})$ and $(I^n\times I,J_n)$ are homeomorphic. A homeomorphism is a continuous bijection with continuous inverse. A homeomorphism of pairs means a homeomorphism of the ambient spaces carrying the specified subspace onto the specified subspace; no pointwise fixing of that subspace is asserted.
